correctness.summary: For an omitted vertex in a multipartite class P_i, the multiset representation contains |S|-s_i copies of distance 1 and s_i copies of distance 2, where s_i=|S∩P_i|. Thus two omitted vertices collide exactly when their s_i values agree. This forces at most one omission per part, and then s_i=n_i-1, so omissions from distinct parts collide exactly when the part sizes agree. The partition-matroid characterization, dimension formula, factored enumerator, and fixed-order spectrum follow. Exhaustive definition-level checks agree on all connected complete-multipartite isomorphism types through order 8.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The inspected 2023 primary source explicitly gives the balanced complete multipartite case and the strictly increasing part-size case, but not arbitrary repeated part sizes. Targeted searches under complete multipartite outer multiset dimension, outer multiset bases, resolving-set counting, and matroid formulations found no equivalent arbitrary-multiplicity classification, partition-matroid description, or factored enumerator. The 2019 foundational work, 2025 joined-graph work, and recent 2026 toroidal-grid work do not supply this general result. Unindexed or differently-termed literature remains a residual risk.

value.summary: The result closes the gap between the previously recorded all-equal and all-distinct complete-multipartite regimes and gives substantially more than the minimum size: it characterizes every resolving set, identifies a partition-matroid mechanism, factors the complete size enumerator, counts all bases, and determines the full fixed-order spectrum within the family.

limitations: The theorem is restricted to complete multipartite graphs.
It does not cover multipartite graphs with missing cross-edges or arbitrary joins.
Real-rootedness is only claimed for the explicitly factored enumerator in this family.
Finite computation supports but does not replace the proof.
Unindexed recent work or older literature under substantially different terminology remains a residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
